As another reviewer stated when pipe was fully stretched by it came to a little over 7 feet.  That was critical as my distance needed was eight feet as my duct joins at the ceiling so we needed to go  buy a short length of  metal pipe to make the  8 feet.  At over a dollar a foot for alum/ flex vinyl , i would at least expect to be not shortchanged  as first few inches at each end are not usable from poor cutting at factory and then you don't even get the 8 feet you paid for.  The package it came in had a zip tie to keep it compressed so I don't think someone would chop off a foot of pipe and zip tie it up again.

I want to clarify, you DO NOT need filters, the filters only give a smoother cup of joe. Filters aren't expensive either, it's 10-15 bucks for 100 of them. I originally bought these so that my parents could use their own coffee in the Keurig. Since there were three in the pack, I put one aside for tea bags. We use them daily and I am delighted with the convenience! I really love throwing my favorite teabag in there (minus the tag) and brewing flavored tea. If you do use them for teabags, just fold the teabag over and try to get it as flat on the bottom as you can (so that the water actually flows through the tea). I have had 1 cup that it must have not hit the tea bag right and it was a bit weak. But most of the time, it is fantastic, My next stop is loose tea...I suspect that it will still work quite well (even if I have to use the strong setting). The only drawback is opening it. The tab is not obvious so I usually have to slide my nail under it to pop it open (probably, because my vision is not great).

The threepack was perfect and I am glad that I didn't just buy a single reusable K Cup. Disclaimer: I am not a coffee or tea connoisseur. The Keurig and these Reusable K Cups are about convenience and a quick cup of tea/coffee.

I washed the plastic strainer piece off and inserted it in the reusable filter, added the ground coffee, and finally got a perfect cup of joe.  Haven't had to use the filter since.

I have an assortment of disposable K-cup beverages for when we have guests. I like for people to have a choice. But for me? I want my favorite coffee every morning, and the easiest and most economical way to have that coffee is to buy it by the pound, so I have several reusable K-cups. I have one red, two purple, and two black and gold. The black and gold ones look fancy, but they don’t work any better than the others. In fact, this K-cup from Nature’s Kitchen is probably the best quality of all I have. It’s sturdier, especially the material on the sides of the cup. No lead or BPA, so I can be confident that I’m not adding chemicals to my coffee. I love the little scoop. I’ve been using a measuring spoon because the standard coffee scoop is too large for a K-cup, but this will be perfect. I really can’t see any reason to use the filters. I tried once, but I don’ t think the coffee was better.

It worked fine for about a month - no problems whatsoever, and great to skip buying pods and just use my favorite coffee. Then it started getting finicky - I'd have to jiggle it in the Keurig and try a few times before I could brew without getting an "oops - this pod wasn't designed for this machine" error message. Clean up is simple, just dump the used grounds in the trash (or put them in the compost pile if you're into that kind of thing), rinse and it's ready to go again!

Extremely high quality and works very well without the need for disposable filters. HOWEVER, it worked flawlessly for about 6 months or a year. I noticed that the water started taking longer and longer to pass through it. Finally, the water would just sit on the top sieve for hours without filtering through.

I washed it, scrubbed it but little changed. I finally figured out that the inside fine screen was getting sediment buildup between the inner and outer screens. The only way I found to partially alleviate the problem was to quite briskly tap the large end on a counter many times, rinsing in between taps. This would partially clear the clog. However, after a few days of use, the water would stop filtering through it. I started using paper liners and it did help a little but after 2-3 years the Marvellissimo Coffee Dripper is useless. Water just sits in the top for hours and hours.
Perfect! Makes a nice strong cup of coffee, with all the flavor and oils. No more running out of paper filters, or toxic chemical paper tasting coffee!

Wow! I'm impressed. Replacing a broken porcelain single dripper and thought I try something new. Great decision. This thing makes a great cup of coffee, is easy to clean and no paper filter taste. Highly recommended!

Feb 29th, 2016: I'm editing this review to add that my coffee filter is becoming clogged and dripping slower over time, like those of a couple of other reviewers. The cone is a double layer of steel mesh, and apparently the grounds get between the layers even if you rinse the cone immediately after you finish brewing. (I've been washing it out before I even drink my coffee.) Maybe a design change would help, or you may want to avoid using finely-ground beans. I noticed that the website of that major coffee shop chain recommends this product called Cafiza for cleaning coffee brewing gear --http://www.amazon.com/Urnex-Cafiza-Espresso-Machine-Cleaner/dp/B001418KNS -- I may try that. Meanwhile, I've lowered my star-rating to four, from five, for the clogging issue. The original review follows.

I like this steel coffee dripper a lot. I've had very tasty coffee from it. (It took a bit of trial and error to get the quantity of coffee right.) Note that the cone is a separate piece from the stand that sits on the top of your cup, and only the cone is dishwasher-safe. The bottom piece that the cone stands on - I'll call it the rack - has a shiny finish, which would probably get wrecked by dishwasher detergent. I am not certain of that, but the paper that came with the item from the seller says not to wash the rack in the dishwasher. The one thing I would change about this product is that the ring of steel that is near the bottom plate of the rack should be welded o

Cleanup - quick and easy, tap used grounds into garbage and rinse.
Portion - easy to see into cup to know how much more water to add.
Green - I like my K-machine but putting those plastic cups in the garbage rubs me the wrong way.
Convenient - I also like my Aero but this product is easier: no filter, no pressing

This pour over coffee cone is exactly what I wanted, but it does pour through slightly faster than I would like. But it makes a decent cup, is not prone to breakage like other models, and allows me to stop using disposable filters. Like the name says, it is indeed marvelissimo :)
Also works well for making bulk batches. Not into making coffee every morning, so I use this to filter into a pitcher. Very good at removing grinds.

At this point I am very happy with my Coffee Dripper.  I have long been searching for the instrument to make the perfect cup of coffee.  This is as close to perfect as I can get.  It took a while to get used to using it, but now I wouldn't use anything else.
Love it! Excellent. Use it every day!! kurig to the curb!!
I totally love this product and I am very pleased with it.
Just exactly what I wanted. I have an old plastic Melitta pour-over that I have tried to duplicate. None of them make as rich a cup of coffee as this one. Highly recommended.
This is so much better than having to make a whole pot of coffee!  I love this product.  It's so simple to use.  And the coffee tastes great.

I've had this for a few weekends now, and I really do love it.  It's a perfect low-cost solution for weekend coffee at home; I drink coffee at work during the week.  The cleanup is really easy, and the results are tasty.  And don't worry about all the fussy directions--I've found that results are consistently good if I just use a fine grind.  I like lots of flavor, but very little caffeine, so I use about 3 tablespoons of fine Vienna Roast Decaf from my local coffee company for each 8 oz. cup--perfect.  But when I use a medium grind the water runs through too quickly, making for a weak brew that is almost as bad as my parent's Maxwell House drip.
Works great with no grounds in the coffee.  Easy to clean and rinse out.  Great for pour-over method of coffee.  I use it to make a single or double cup at a time.
Awesome filter!  I can't believe I was putting up with the Keurig for so long....  This takes literally an additional 3 or so minutes - what was I thinking?
Clogged up after about a month. Could't clean out the holes.
gets clogged every time. Terrible
Excellent filter. I use it to filter my cold brew coffee. Does a great job of getting out any fine particles so there is no silt left. Very easy to clean.

It works. Cleaning problems? Just rinse it with hot water right after using. Don't set it aside to get crusty! Rinse the hot water tap onto it from the OUTSIDE to push the crud back out from how it came in. Quick & easy. Makes good coffee with mouth feel.No nasty paper flavors. Yum.

I love the drip coffee process. I have no earthly idea why I've spent the money that I have over the years on coffeepots & coffeemakers. This is the best coffee ever with the simplest process. I think it's because there's nowhere for the water to sit and get old etc. etc.
Exsselent!
I enjoy having a variety of tools for my daily coffee, this is one of many I own, it is exactly what I expected

I bought this since I was having numerous breakthroughs with paper filters. The mesh on this is perfect - no grounds will get through this but the coffee flows perfectly. You do have to be a bit careful with pouring since the filter holes go all the way up the side of the cone. It's really not a problem, just something to be aware of.
I was most impressed with the company's passion for it's product and making sure I understood how to use it even before I received it! I would definitely recommend this to other people.

I'm all about reducing and refusing single use, so this little unit is perfect for me. Save money on filters (mine has paid for itself already) and it makes a great cup of coffee. Can be a bit messy, so find a cute bowl to catch drippings. I usually make a second cup by adding more ground coffee to the existing grounds, and it still tastes great and does not clog. It's easy to clean by hand but probably would be fine on the top rack of the dishwasher.

this is well made, and the inner mesh is very fine. I get a tiny bit of residue in my cup, but nothing to worry about. I have found, while using it, that I can actually use less coffee, as the flavor of the coffee is so pure. I would definitely recommend this product.
Great product....would buy for friends/gifts.  Easy clean and never have to buy paper filters

Just made my first cup. WOW! This is/was GREAT! A wholly different experience and I LOVED IT! Beyond a "great cup of coffee."  This strainer worked super, cleaned easily and opened a new world for me. Thank you!.  Nice and sturdy, heavy SS construction, "just right" for this job. No disappointment here.

Works great when new! I bought it to filter the sediment in French-press coffee. To be fair, the filter might not have been designed for this purpose. However, after a few months of daily use, the filter is almost completely clogged. Unfortunately, the filter cannot be disassembled to clean between the layers.  I would have given this product a higher rating when new.

Was great for the first 20 or so uses and now it doesn't work.  After several attempts to clean it, the filter no longer filters anything, it only provides approximately one drip per 20 minute!  Great concept but disappointing.
gets clogged - disasspointing
Great coffee; it is smaller than I would like.  It takes a long time to get two cups brewed.

So, this is a good quality product, however... I have two issues with it. First, the rim on the cone holder, where it sits on top of the cup, is too dang small. I like my big oversized coffee cups and it sits on top of them very tentatively and already have tipped it getting coffee everywhere. That being said, it fits fine on smaller probably more typical cups. However, the manufacturer should indicate this and also consider increasing the size of the base because large cups are very common now.

Second, I find the coffee is better if I still put a paper filter in. I rinse it first with boiling water, then put the coffee in. Otherwise, the water goes too fast through the coffee and metal mesh (without the paper) and my coffee is always too weak. This is with a regular grind. Perhaps if I did a finer grind it would work better.

Update: ok i have HAD it with this filter. Today it tipped because the rim is TOO SMALL and I burned my hand on the boiling hot wet coffee grounds trying to stop it from flying everywhere which it did anyway. I'm sorry it's a nice product but its bloody dangerous. It needs a bigger rim for the top of a cup. Admittedly this is written out of anger grrrr (pain) grrr

The stand doesn't have a flange on the base like my old Melitta plastic filter holder which is what I wanted because it sits flat on the new insulated mug I bought. The stainless steel mesh is very fine and keeps the sludge out of my cup unlike the previous mesh filter cone I had. It cleans easily and drips fairly fast depending on the fineness of the coffee grounds. I am happy with it!

Love this product! No more potential chemicals from paper filters or messy clean-up of cloth filters . . . and no metallic taste! We've found the dripper we'll be using permanently. Love the easy clean-up -- so easy to rinse and swish with soapy water. Thank you!

Works very well, very well made, great value. I can't help but wonder if the frame should be permanently attached to the cone or if the frame should have a tab for easier moving together with the cone i.e. when moving to clean it. Thank you.

This Marvellissimo Coffee filter is excellent.  Coffee grains do not get stuck in the meshing, it washes out clean looks and like new.  I've been using mine for 3 weeks and love it.  The only improvement I could suggest is a larger one for making a full pot of coffee!

This filter was great the first 2 weeks that I used it. After then, it became clogged and now takes 20+ minutes to brew a cup of coffee, plus it smells like old coffee grinds. I have tried rinsing it, soaking it, and scrubbing it, but nothing seems to get the tiny grinds out from between the two layers. I was really excited and happy when I first tried this thing out, but now I'm just frustrated. Great concept, but if I could go back, I'd use it with a paper coffee filter to prevent the clogging between the two layers.
Could not get coffee grounds unclogged and would not work after a few uses.
At first I used this product and thought it was awesome. Great coffee after about five minutes. After a week, however, it now takes 30-40 minutes to filter through. I regret making this purchase.

Like many other reviewers, I loved it at first.  Unfortunately fine grounds get between the two layers and no amount of brushing, boiling, spraying, scrubbing with baking soda, will unclog it.  At the time I purchased it, price was $10 higher, about $25.  I probably got 6 weeks of filterless use out of it.  By using paper filters to speed it up, I continued to use for several months until it would barely drip.  Now I'm back to using a ceramic over-cup dripper for a delicious, frustration free morning java.

I wanted to love these. I purchased 7 of them to use at our bakery. We have been using them for less than a month (maybe once a day each) and they are all stopped up. They are washed thoroughly after use but the dripping is pretty much nonexistent now. Our customers don't want to wait 10 minutes for their coffee. I am unsure if I got a bad batch of these or what but I am now going to have to explore other options. This was a huge waste of money and now I can't return them.

It's a little bigger than I thought but it works fine. Not happy that it came apart within 6 months. The ring fell off completely and seam the holds cone together is coming undone. It has not been abused but has been used to make two cups every day...

It's not awful, but it's the slowest coffee dripper I've ever used. The metal holes are just so small, they get clogged. I had to stir coffee in this while it was seeping multiple times. It works- it's just not what I wanted.
Love it

It works great for few uses and then it starts to clog. Coffee would drip through really slow, slower than normal, and then it stops dripping half way. Tried to clean it a few times, still clogging. I like it but I would not but it again.

Just as other reviewers have stated, the filter now is blocked up and it takes a good 10 minutes to make a cup of coffee. And I am using coarse grounds. A year supply of paper filters for a miletta is around $4 which means this ought to last 4-5 years to be more economical. It lasted me 2 months.

I agree with the other one star reviews. This worked great for about 2-3 weeks then stopped dripping coffee despite my attempts to clean it with a wire brush, baking soda, and vinegar. There is not way to take it apart to clean the inner lining. I would not recommend this product.
Works better with a paper filter insert.

It's ok. Does the job. Very difficult to get grounds out of cone. They seem to stick fiercely to sides. Bulky and rather odd looking just sitting in my kitchen but like I said IT DOES THE JOB. I was supposed to be reimbursed for product but still waiting.

The product simply does not work. You load a bit of ground coffee in, pour in hot water, and the water does not get through it. It just pools up, and only one drop of coffee drips through each second. If you can wait one hour for your coffee, and then reheat it, maybe this product is for you.

makes a good single cup of coffee.

I just bought a ceramic one to replace it.  I will have to use paper filters, but at least I will get a cup of hot coffee out of it in less than 30 minutes!
